claims.claim: Gennadius was Patriarch of Constantinople from 458 to 471.
Gennadius wrote commentaries on all the epistles of St. Paul, but only a few fragments remain.
Gennadius's Pauline commentary fragments are collected in Migne, Patrologia Graeca, LXXXV.
Some fragments of Gennadius's biblical works are found in the catena of Oecumenius and the catena of Nikephoros Kallistos Xanthopoulos.
A few fragments of Gennadius's works are found in the Vienna MS. gr. 166 (46).
Gennadius followed the Antiochene school of literal exegesis.
Gennadius was a champion of Christian Orthodoxy who strove to reconcile the opposing Alexandrian and Antiochene theological traditions.
As a young man, Gennadius vigorously attacked Cyril of Alexandria's Twelve Anathemas in 431.
Gennadius became patriarch in 458 and, with Pope Leo I's counsel, proceeded against the Monophysites and deposed their titular head, Bishop Timotheus Aelurus of Alexandria.
Gennadius's surviving fragments are interesting specimens of 5th century exegesis.
